newsitem.title: INDIA: Pre-budget India stocks show optimism building.
newsitem.headline: Pre-budget India stocks show optimism building.

text.p: Cautious optimism showed in lively pre-budget sessions on Indian stock markets on Friday as traders made last minute deals before Finance Minister P.Chidambaram delivered his 1997/98 package. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top 30 index was up a provisional 48.45 points or 1.41 percent, at 3,476.32 when it ended the first session of trading, before re-opening for a special post-budget session.
An early surge had seen the index show a 2.4 percent gain before profit-taking set in.
The BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were due to resume trading for two hours at 6 p.m. (1230 GMT) for a special evening session an hour after Chidambaram was set to start his speech.
"People are cautiously optimistic. I think the market view is equally divided," said Gul Teckchandani, chief investment officer at Sun Foreign & Colonial Asset Management.
The budget is seen as a litmus test for Chidambaram, who has to cope with the political compulsions of a fractious 15-party centre-left coalition.
"Clearly, we are looking for policy statements on whether the government means that reforms will be carried forward," Teckchandani said.
Some analysts said creeping market optimism that the government would announce strong steps in the budget to revive a slowing economy and boost markets helped stoke renewed hopes.
Most analysts believe he will be unable to introduce any radical budgetary measures to cut expenditure.
"My expectation from the budget is not of policy announcements, it's more of implementation," said Subra Subramanian, India research director at foreign securities firm H.G. Asia.

The market is looking for a jettisoning of double taxation on company dividends, and freedom for firms to buy back their own shares. There is also hope for a reduction of a 7.5 percent corporate surcharge and a revamped minimum alternate tax.
"The levels of expectation are very low. There is a very small downward risk at this stage," said chief dealer Sanjay Vaid at Lloyds Securities, a local firm.
The NSE finished its early session at 998.65, up 5.90 points or 0.59 percent.
Both markets will open on Saturday for another special post-budget trading session.
